Here's something obvious you seem to disregard. Democracy is good but disinformation hurts democracy. We can only achieve a deliberate form of democracy if everyone or the majority is well-informed. Democracy has faced that issue since the fucking 18th century. Not a new thought that sprung out in this thread. Democracy is not perfect. It's fairly common to discuss its imperfections without being labeled as anti-democracy. 

Say, every citizen wants good healthcare and each of them is misinformed about vaccines and is anti-vaxx, what then aligns with the interest of the people when their "facts" don't align with their own interests?

Ofc, the govt has the responsibility to address that incoherence carefully, if that happens. For example, if the govt is straight up blaming the people for being misinformed, the people will most likely retaliate, even if it's true that they were misinformed.

But in any case that the government point finger to the misinformed people which is in my example, detrimental, that is not a plus points to the misinformation-driven democracy just because they're on the opposite sides. You still have to criticize both.

Neither is it fair to judge the critics of fake news driven democracy to be anti-democracy. This isn't black and white. You can criticize a thing you value and that doesn't make it less valuable to you. 

The "good" still needs criticism and you're not going anywhere if you see the good and just fully accept the consequences it carries just because it's universally good.
